name: What’s the best way to budget contingency for a ground-up build?

mainEntity.name: How much contingency should be set aside for unexpected costs on a Los Angeles custom home?
mainEntity.text: How much contingency should be set aside for unexpected costs on a Los Angeles custom home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Contingency is essential in ground-up construction because even well-planned projects encounter surprises. The amount needed depends on how complicated the lot and design are. Flat lots with straightforward plans may need a smaller reserve, while hillside, coastal, or highly customized homes need more. Typical surprises include soil conditions, utility changes, design revisions, material price shifts, and permit comments that affect scope. Contingency should be treated as a separate line item rather than money that gets absorbed into the base budget. That makes it easier to make decisions when unexpected costs appear. Owners should also protect the contingency by avoiding unnecessary upgrades after pricing and by finalizing the design before construction starts. The goal is not to eliminate surprises, but to make sure they do not stall the project or force compromises later.

Contingency should be separate from the base construction budget so unexpected items do not derail the project.
